invariants.rationale: The method always returns a non-null Iterator either from superclass or from a singleton list, so result is never null.
The returned Iterator conforms to Java's Iterator contract and must implement hasNext().
partitionPath is passed as an argument and used to construct handles and delegate; there is no reason for it to be null.
fileId is passed as argument, used in logging and handle creation, so should be non-null at exit.
recordItr, as a parameter, is always an Iterator and will always be usable at exit as per Java semantics.
